To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified a novel gene expression–based predictor for neuroblastoma patient outcome that outperformed established clinical prognostic markers in multivariate Cox regression analyses.

we developed a gene expression–based classifier that outperforms established risk assessment for low-risk/ intermediate-risk neuroblastoma patients and that we propose a revised risk stratified treatment approach that may help to improve treatment outcome of these patients.

we have developed a new risk estimation system by combining gene expression–based classifiers and clinical prognostic markers for neuroblastoma, which improves treatment stratification for patients with low- and intermediate-risk neuroblastoma, and which we propose to implement in a prospective clinical study.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of molecular markers that can be used to predict the clinical outcome of patients with neuroblastoma, a common childhood malignancy.
the development of new prognostic markers for neuroblastoma, which are based on the analysis of the tumor transcriptome (gene expression profile).
the identification of novel prognostic markers and their integration into a revised risk estimation and treatment stratification system for neuroblastoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the current risk classification of neuroblastoma, as defined in the International Neuroblastoma Risk Group (INRG) classification, is not sufficient to identify all patients with a favorable or unfavorable outcome, especially in the low- and intermediate-risk group.
the authors have developed a new classification system that is superior to the current one.
the authors have developed an improved prognostic classifier for patients with neuroblastoma that has the potential to improve treatment stratification.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a gene expression–based predictor that can be used to identify patients with low-risk and intermediate-risk neuroblastoma, who have a high risk of relapse or poor outcome.
we have identified a new molecular prognostic marker that is superior to all previously described prognostic markers for neuroblastoma.
we were able to develop a novel prognostic model for patients with low- and intermediate-risk neuroblastoma by combining gene expression–based classifiers and established clinical markers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gene expression–based risk stratification of low-risk and intermediate-risk neuroblastoma patients is feasible and may improve treatment stratification of patients with neuroblastoma.
the current treatment stratification of low- and intermediate-risk patients in the NB2004 trial is suboptimal.

we have shown that it is possible to integrate clinical prognostic factors, such as stage of disease and MYCN amplification status, with molecular prognostic markers, such as gene expression signatures, to improve the accuracy of risk estimation in patients with neuroblastoma.
